claims: A false imprisonment charge involves the intentional, unlawful restriction of another person’s freedom of movement without their consent or legal authority.
False arrest is typically used when police or authority acts without warrant.
Kidnapping is a more severe form often involving movement.
False imprisonment does not require movement.
False imprisonment requires that the perpetrator must have intended to confine the victim.
False imprisonment requires that the restraint was done against the victim's will.
False imprisonment requires that the act was not legally justified.
Misdemeanor charges may result in up to 1 year in jail.
Felonies can lead to 3 or more years in prison depending on the jurisdiction and use of violence or fraud.
A store owner detaining a customer without reasonable suspicion of theft exceeds shopkeeper's privilege.
